summary: This case study details a lease-based, zero-trust test sharding scheduler that offloads local CI suites across idle Apple-silicon Macs on a local network to relieve a saturated controller machine. The system demonstrates practical engineering solutions for local compute scavenging, including Git object transport, greedy LPT scheduling, late-join queues, and failure isolation, while providing concrete performance gains.
strengths: High practical value for engineering teams running intensive local CI pipelines or agentic coding loops on Apple-silicon hardware
Pragmatic security and failure isolation model: runners cannot issue authoritative failures, receive no credentials, and execute detached Git worktrees
Detailed documentation of subtle real-world edge cases, including accounting for sibling lane processes during CPU probes and preventing asynchronous Node.js pipe write truncation on process exit
Honest discussion of methodology and operational limitations, specifically acknowledging small sample sizes and network environment factors
weaknesses: No public repository or reusable tool artifact provided, limiting direct reproducibility to code snippets and architectural patterns
Evaluations were performed in non-interleaved runs under varying uncontrolled agent background loads, meaning benchmark numbers are indicative rather than statistically rigorous
suggestions: Extract the scheduling scripts, probe routines, and lease managers into an open-source utility repository to enable full community reproducibility
Run systematic benchmark trials under controlled synthetic CPU loads to measure latency improvements and variance with formal confidence intervals

claims.text: The split is Graham's LPT heuristic (Graham, 1969, "Bounds on multiprocessing timing anomalies", SIAM J. Appl. Math.).
Condor (Litzkow, Livny and Mutka, 1988, "Condor: a hunter of idle workstations", ICDCS) scheduled jobs on idle machines and evicted them when owners returned.
`rr` (github.com/rileyhilliard/rr) syncs a working tree to SSH hosts, locks a free host and runs shards in parallel.
On macOS, stdout to a pipe is asynchronous, so the process.exit() after the end of input dropped whatever was still queued.

novelty_vs_existing.title: rr: Easily sync code to a remote machine and run commands there
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Adds load-probed CPU/memory leasing, automated Git object push rather than rsync trees, LPT test-timing sharding, a dynamic late-join queue, and strict fallback-to-local failure arbitration

novelty_vs_existing.title: Condor: A Hunter of Idle Workstations
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Adapts classical workstation cycle scavenging specifically to modern local test runner suites (Vitest, PostgreSQL) on Apple-silicon Macs with unmanaged desktop workers and zero credential sharing
